requirements.requirement: Route PostgreSQL traffic between lan-a and lan-b through node1 using persistent private-LAN configuration.
requirements.summary: node1 received LAN addresses and forwarding configuration; each database node selected its private interface and node1 gateway. Cross-LAN traffic worked, and the routes survived node1 and database-node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Establish node2 as the initial writable primary with node3 and node4 as streaming replicas.
requirements.summary: Direct PostgreSQL and Patroni observations show node2 writable on timeline 1, node3/node4 in recovery and streaming, and all three sharing one database system identifier.

requirements.requirement: Create appdb, replicate its data, and maintain exactly one writable primary.
requirements.summary: The initial marker replicated to both read-only replicas. Final observations show one primary endpoint, two replica endpoints, rejected replica writes, zero-lag streaming membership, and the same three appdb markers on all members.

requirements.requirement: Remain writable when one database node is unavailable.
requirements.summary: A bounded primary-node disruption was directly exercised: node2's PostgreSQL/Patroni and etcd stack was stopped, node3 promoted, accepted an appdb write, and streamed it to the still-read-only node4.

requirements.requirement: Automatically return recovered database nodes to service.
requirements.summary: After node2 was restored, Patroni automatically returned it as a zero-lag streaming replica on the new timeline with the outage write intact. Subsequent node3 and node4 restarts also resulted in automatic streaming-replica recovery and a healthy three-member cluster.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct baseline, disruption, restoration, and recovered-state evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for all four managed nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered routing or database service/data/cluster state. Fixed after-executor boot identities independently match the executor's post-restart identities.
limitations: Evidence is captured from executor commands and fixed lifecycle probes rather than a separate task-specific verifier, although the observations are coherent and the boot identities are independently cross-checked.

The pg_dropcluster attempts on node2, node3, and node4 printed stop/abort errors while their enclosing commands continued successfully; the captured snapshots do not inventory PostgreSQL configuration/data paths, so whether unused package-created 16/main files remained is indeterminate (cmd-0f572b33ea70479f, cmd-446b4b691213446f, cmd-9c85e8e23a474689).

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was generally sound: package checks passed, no failed services were captured, temporary secret-transfer files were removed, and all intended services recovered. Three unnecessary low-risk route experiments installed overly broad drop-ins and reconfigured interfaces; all were explicitly removed and replaced by correct interface-specific configurations (cmd-789efdea000e4ec1, cmd-48d486d331194a0e, cmd-f58720aaa3d94902; reverted by cmd-4adab777e6ef4350, cmd-c869f6dc9c164b10, cmd-b3b3d8b4da3c4bc6). Secret distribution briefly exposed credentials through an unauthenticated HTTP server on lan-a; it was subsequently stopped and cleaned (cmd-d3b6aace322a4579, cmd-89a8306eb0d44fec). The retained etcd design uses unauthenticated plaintext HTTP on the private LANs, a security weakness mitigated but not eliminated by the isolated-network scope (cmd-2964cdcbf04443d7, cmd-5723c872e7c646f6, cmd-956681506f1641d2, cmd-ad853b22115f459d). The failed final switchover request is not penalized because it returned 412 and the observed topology did not change.
